title: Book One · Chapter 177: A Seat by the Door
story:
Mr Qiu returns and stops in the doorway.

He looks at the room before he comes in. Ronan sees his eyes move from the map to the drawings, then to the little table of objects.

“You have been busy.”

“Come and see your part,” Ronan says.

Mr Qiu takes a step. Then he puts one hand against the wall.

“A moment.”

Ronan looks at the map. There is a place for Mr Qiu near the river. Mei has drawn the rows of paper and pencils very carefully.

He wants to show him now.

Then he sees the stool.

“You can sit here.”

Mr Qiu looks down at it.

“May I sit on it?”

“Yes. It is a safe seat.”

Ronan moves the card a little farther back on its table, clear of the man's sleeve.

Mr Qiu sits slowly. He rests both hands on his knees.

“Your dad fixed this?”

“Yes.”

“He did a good job.”

Ronan looks at the legs. All four stand on the floor.

Leo comes over. He has a small drawing in one hand.

“We can bring your part here,” he tells Mr Qiu.

Mei takes one end of the drawing. They hold it between them, low enough for him to see.

Mr Qiu points to a line near the corner.

“That shelf is a little higher.”

“It used to be,” Mei says. “You moved it.”

Mr Qiu looks again.

Then he laughs.

“You are right. I see the old place in my head sometimes.”

Ronan remembers their old home too. Sometimes he wakes and expects to see the old tree. Then he remembers his home by the green gate.

“We can put an old picture beside this one,” he says.

“Another day,” Mei tells him. “This one is already finished.”

Ronan nods. He does not go to get new paper.

Mr Qiu looks at the small words under the drawing.

“You asked me before you wrote these.”

“Yes.”

“Thank you.”

A woman waits to come through the door. Ronan moves a bag and holds the door for her.

She has a small child by the hand. The child sees the stool and wants to climb on Mr Qiu’s knee.

“Not today,” the woman says gently.

She bends down and speaks quietly. The child sits on the floor beside her instead.

Mr Qiu watches the map from his seat. Now and then, he explains a line to someone. He points to the place on the map.

Soon, he is helping too.

Mum comes over with a cup of water. “Where can I put your water?” she asks.

“Here is fine,” he says.

She puts it on a clear part of the table, away from the paper.

Ronan looks toward the hall again.

Mr Qiu sees him looking.

“Your father?”

Ronan nods.

“He is at work.”

“Yes.”

Mr Qiu does not say, “Your dad will certainly come.” He drinks a little water.

“You can show him later if you need to.”

“I know.”

A visitor asks about a shop on the map. Ronan goes to answer. From that side of the table, he can still see the stool.

Someone is using the stool now. Other people can still walk past it and reach the map.

Mr Qiu sits there and talks about the street. A small child listens. Leo stands beside him. Mei brings another drawing.

Ronan watches for a moment.

Then he turns to the visitor.

“Which place do you want to find?”

Before three, Mr Qiu stands up. He must open his table again at the time on his sign. Mum brings his bag. He pats the stool and thanks them. The empty pencil box stays on its table. They will give it back after the display.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达
- rest：休息；也可表示把手放在某处。
- certainly：肯定、一定。
- instead：改为、代替。
- clear：没有东西挡着的。

## 理解
1. Ronan 怎样让Mr Qiu参与展示？
2. Mei 为什么没有马上同意增加一张画？
